terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: primaryDomain=character. Secondary read hybrid: the hair is authored as a hard-surface, cuboid faceted shell (Minecraft-like blocks plus lateral ear-cup slabs) sitting on a soft organic chibi skull. The body is a normal chibi humanoid in a standing A-pose; the hair shell must NOT be smoothed into organic locks. Identity is carried by the hair silhouette, the blank ringed eyes and the black/white two-value outfit.

reasoning: silhouetteComplexity=3: the twin-tails plus the blocky hair shell interrupt the outline at every height; the widest point (795px at y=346) is hair, not body.
componentCount=3: seven macro parts, each with meso sub-parts, plus two mirrored limbs and two mirrored tails.
hierarchyDepth=3: root -> assembly -> sub-part -> feature group is required (e.g. torso -> coat -> coat panel -> white edge trim).
repetitionDensity=2: three genuine repetition systems (four tail slabs per side, the coat trim linework chain, the boot chevrons), not thousands of micro marks.
materialLayerCount=2: only seven materials, but several are split into bounded sub-regions (black cloth plus white trim on the same panel).
localDetailDensity=2: bounded hard-edged detail (star, chevrons, buckle, choker ring, eye ring) rather than surface microtexture.
occlusionRisk=2: hood volume, coat interior and the fringe underside are not observable from the sheet.
actionReadinessNeed=2: a rig-ready humanoid needs a joint chain and pivots, but no destruction or effects.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Every macro part of this subject has visible meso sub-parts (the coat alone has panels, hood, trim and star), and three feature families repeat (tail slabs, trim chain, boot chevrons). A root-only or macro-only spec would describe a different, generic chibi.

detailInventory.note: Each detail maps to a component.localFeatures entry, so none is prose-only.

details.description: Thick black limbal ring around each eye, ~13% of the eye diameter, fully enclosing a blank sclera
Hard-edged white five-point star centred on the coat back
White edge linework running the full perimeter of each coat panel opening
Crown is a raised central block flanked by two lower slabs, producing the stepped top edge
Flat rectangular ear-cup plate projecting laterally over the ear position on each side
Square buckle plate centred on the white belt
Small metal ring pendant on the choker at the throat
Nested white V strokes wrapping each boot at ankle height
Light wedge sole under each boot, thicker at the toe, the only bright element below the knee
Navel on the exposed midriff band, between the halter top and the shorts
Four stacked angular slabs per twin tail, tapering distally into a notched fan
A fringe lock overlaps the character's left eye, cutting its visible width to 52 px from 69 px
White band where each sleeve meets its glove, plus an upper-arm band
Raised collar band at the throat with a small zipper pull at its centre front

pose.type: standing A-pose, symmetric, arms abducted ~28 degrees, legs straight and slightly apart

features: chibi head-to-body ratio 2.6 HU (crown 165, chin 488, ground 1017)
blank white ringed eyes centred at (356,417) and (497,417), 62px diameter, 81px inner-corner gap
blocky faceted hair shell spanning x[240..609] y[165..488]
anatomy.measurementNotes: Face landmarks are normalised to the head+hair bounding box, so eyeLine reads low (0.78) because the hair mass occupies the upper 60% of that box. This is the measured value. screen-x and screen-y here are reference-sheet axes; the model must use 3D object space with forward=+Z, up=+Y and the character's own left=+X.

definitionOfDone: The render reads as THIS chibi at a glance: ~2.6 HU head-dominated silhouette, two long segmented twin-tails that terminate above the boot tops, and a hard-edged blocky hair shell that is never smoothed into organic locks.

The face carries the two identity-defining eyes: large blank white discs inside a thick black limbal ring, with no iris and no pupil, plus the asymmetric fringe lock that overlaps the character's left eye.

Every white accent on the black garment is a bounded GEOMETRY region (vertex-painted region / separate shell), never a painted texture: the coat trim chain, the back star, the belt, the boot chevrons and the sleeve bands.
The exposed skin regions are the correct three bands: the midriff between halter top and shorts, and the bare thigh band between shorts and boot tops.
The model is an action-ready hierarchy: named pivot joints (root, neck, head, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles, tail roots), every mesh bound to its parent rather than floating.

featureGroups.name: Chibi proportion and stance
qualityCriteria: Head unit (cranium+hair block) is 2.6 heads of total height; head width 369px at reference scale is wider than the shoulder width 242px.
Legs measure 0.84 HU hip-to-ground; shoulders 0.75 HU; hips 0.62 HU.
Arms are abducted ~28 degrees and the stance is symmetric, matching the front view silhouette.

featureGroups.name: Faceted blocky hair shell
qualityCriteria: Hair is built from flat cuboid slabs with visible facet-to-facet value steps, a raised central crown block flanked by lower slabs, and a flat lateral ear-cup plate on each side.
No smoothing modifier, no organic lock geometry, no strand cards: the reference is deliberately hard-surface.
Roots bind to the scalp surface, and the shell reads as one connected mass rather than floating boxes.
failureModes: hair slabs floating off the skull

featureGroups.name: Long segmented twin-tails
qualityCriteria: Each tail is a chain of four stacked angular slabs whose widths taper distally, ending in a notched spiky fan.
Tail length reaches to y~810 at reference scale, i.e. below the hip and above the boot top - not to the ankles.
Roots sit at azimuth +/-90 degrees on the head at ear-cup height; the two tails are exact mirror images ((-x,y,z) reflection, not a rotation).
failureModes: straight cones instead of segmented slabs

featureGroups.name: Blank ringed eyes
qualityCriteria: Each eye is a bright white disc of 62px reference diameter inside a thick black ring, with no iris and no pupil.
Eye centres are at 141px separation and 81px inner-corner gap, vertically at 0.78 of the head box.
The character's left eye is partially covered by a fringe lock so its visible width is smaller than the other.

featureGroups.name: Black outfit with white bounded trim
qualityCriteria: Coat trim runs continuously along the collar, the two front panel openings and the hem; the back carries a hard-edged five-point white star.
Belt with a square buckle at the waist, white chevrons at each boot ankle, white wrist and upper-arm bands.
Each white mark is a bounded region with a clean boundary on the black cloth - no gradient, no noise, no painted texture map.
failureModes: trim lines crossing each other wrongly

featureGroups.name: Reference material response
qualityCriteria: Skin: warm pale albedo, roughness ~0.55, no transmission.
Hair and black cloth: matte-to-satin, roughness ~0.42-0.50, broad low-frequency sheen only - no strand specular, no gloss.
White trim is matte (~0.45 roughness), not glowing; the only metal is the belt buckle and choker ring (metalness ~0.75).
Every white accent is verified on GEOMETRY, not on a texture, so it survives a relight.

visualDeltaChecks: silhouette delta at head, shoulder, hip and boot-top heights

antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if the spec collapses the seven macro parts into a root-only tree.
Do not represent any white accent only in prose or only as a texture.
Do not smooth the hair shell to make it look 'better' - the blockiness is the identity feature.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, embedDepth and gapTolerance.
Adjacent components must overlap by at least 0.02 world units at shared seams (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Raised or recessed relief and fasteners must be geometry, instanced micro-parts, or displacement; a map alone is an approximation (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Blank ringed eyes and face landmarks
Blocky hair shell and ear cups

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.
lookDevTargets.qualityPriorityRationale: Flat-paint stylized subject. Surface identity is carried by bounded colour regions and by silhouette, not by grain, print or pores, so the texture-channel bar does not describe this model. Materials are declared textureless with per-material evidence.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro and meso component is emitted as a named Object3D pivot Group with a mesh child, an action profile, collider proxy and destruction metadata. Bone-track skinning is deliberately not emitted: this subject's identity is bounded flat regions and rigid blocky hair, so a pivot hierarchy preserves it and a skeleton whose bind pose was authored for a different proportion set would only distort it.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Stylized reconstruction from a three-view sheet; hidden sides and the coat interior are inferred, never measured.
Twin-tail cross-section is read as a flattened rectilinear ribbon (confidence 0.55).
Hood volume behind the shoulders is inferred from the side view only (confidence 0.5).
Glove finger separation is hidden in all three views and is therefore not invented.
The white accents are authored as bounded geometry regions, matching the reference's hard boundaries.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z is the direction the character faces
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: total crown-to-ground height = 1.0 unit; ground plane at y = 0

silhouette.boundingShape: a narrow vertical column of body flanked by two long tapered tail masses that flare past shoulder width and terminate above the boot tops
silhouette.symmetry: bilateral about the sagittal plane in the front and rear views
negativeSpaces: the open V between the two coat front panels
the gap between the twin tails below the shoulders

observations: Twin-tail length terminates above the boot tops.
Eye whites measured at 62 px diameter, 141 px centre separation.
Head+hair block 369 px wide x 323 px tall on an 852 px figure (2.6 head units).
Confirms the tails are thin through screen-y, so the section is a flattened ribbon.
Shows the boot foot projecting forward past the body depth.
Shows the collapsed hood's outer boundary behind the shoulder.
Confirms the five-point white star centred on the coat back.
Confirms the rear vent split below the star.
Confirms hair slabs are flat and faceted, with no strand structure.

featureReviews.name: Chibi head-unit proportions
featureReviews.notes: Measured landmarks are honoured: ground y=0.000, hip 0.300, shoulder 0.545, chin 0.621, crown 1.000. The head+hair block reads 0.42 wide x 0.37 tall against a 1.0 total height, i.e. 2.6 head units, matching the 369 x 323 px block on the 852 px reference figure.

featureReviews.name: Twin-tail silhouette and pose
featureReviews.notes: Symmetric A-pose, arms abducted 28 degrees off vertical as read from the front silhouette. Both tails flare outward from the head sides and terminate above the boot tops rather than at the ankles. They are untapered single slabs at this pass by construction; the four-slab taper is a meso task at structural-pass.

visualEvidence.notes: Six labelled viewpoints plus an unlit map-stripped silhouette. Silhouette agrees at the head, tail and boot-top heights.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Score is against the blockout acceptance (head-unit proportion and pose silhouette), NOT against the finished character: a macro-only blockout has no face, no garment break-up and no material response by construction, so formDetail and materialSurface are expected to be low. Judged criterion: is the head-dominated 2.6 HU proportion and the symmetric A-pose right. Measurably, yes.

featureReviews.name: Blank ringed eyes and face landmarks
featureReviews.notes: Two large blank white discs sit inside thick black limbal rings, with no iris and no pupil - matching the reference's most distinctive facial feature. Disc diameter 0.073 units against a measured 62 px on an 852 px figure (0.0728). Centres at +/-0.0827 from the midline against a measured 141 px separation (0.1655 total). Eyes sit on the computed ellipsoid surface (z 0.125 at that height) rather than floating in front of it, and the ring torus is the frontmost of the two. The mouth is a 0.045-wide dark line at the measured 0.929 of the head box.

visualEvidence.notes: Six labelled viewpoints. The back view now carries the five-point white star clearly.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Structure is complete: every visible sub-part named in the spec now exists as its own pivot plus mesh, and nothing floats - the attachment endpoints put each limb's pivot on its socket. The remaining gap to the reference is form refinement (tail taper, collar shape) and material response, both scheduled for the next two passes.

featureReviews.name: Twin-tail silhouette and pose
featureReviews.notes: Each tail now reads as a chain of four stacked angular slabs on an outward-then-down arc: the second slab reaches the widest lateral extent and the fourth is narrowest, so the chain tapers distally and terminates above the boot top. The arms keep the measured 28-degree abduction and the stance is symmetric.

featureReviews.name: Blocky hair shell and ear cups
featureReviews.notes: The crown reads as a raised central block flanked by lower slabs, the fringe stops at the measured hairline and no longer covers the eyes, the side locks narrow the visible face to the measured 216 px equivalent, and the lateral ear-cup plates project to the measured 0.216 lateral extent. The two crest spikes rise above the crown as angular blades, not cones. Nothing was smoothed: every hair surface is a flat facet.

visualEvidence.notes: Six labelled viewpoints. First pass where the model is recognisable as the reference character at a glance.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Form now matches the reference's blocky read: nothing is smoothed, the tails taper, and the face is the right size in the right window. Material response is already close because the subject is flat paint, which is why materialSurface is not far behind.

featureReviews.name: Outfit, white accents and palette
featureReviews.notes: Two-value palette matches the reference: near-black garment and hair with a single neutral white accent family. Every white mark is bounded geometry, not a texture - coat panel trim strips, hem trim, the five-point back star, the belt, the boot chevrons and the sleeve bands - so all of them survive a relight. The finish is matte throughout (roughness 0.72-0.85 on the blacks) after the earlier flat-facet specular blowout was traced to an under-rough hair material, not to geometry. The only metal is the belt buckle, the choker ring and the halter ring.

visualEvidence.notes: Six labelled viewpoints. Back star, boot soles, buckle and choker ring all read.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Material response is now the strongest layer, which is expected for a flat-paint subject: the whole palette is seven bounded values and the model reproduces them. The remaining gap is geometric - how much of the belt the coat opening reveals - not a material one.

featureReviews.name: Outfit, white accents and palette

visualEvidence.notes: Eight captures: six labelled viewpoints, a reference-matched light pass and a grazing-light pass.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Lighting is judged on whether material readability survives it, and it does: the neutral, reference-matched and grazing renders all show the same bounded regions, so no white accent is a lighting artefact. This is an approximate stylized reconstruction, not a 100 percent likeness - the hair mass and tail length are the two clearest remaining gaps, and both are recorded above.

visualEvidence.notes: Overlay legend: black = agreement, red = reference only, blue = render only.

A passing visual impression is not proof of silhouette agreement.

risks: DETERMINISTIC GATE FAILURE, stated first because it outranks every visual score above: the pipeline's own Tier 1 diagnostic reports silhouette IoU 0.40-0.47 against a threshold of 0.85 on EVERY pass, and an aspect-ratio delta of 0.067-0.077 against 0.05. The AI-vision reviews were appended BEFORE this gate was run, which is the wrong order (Tier 1 must gate Tier 2), so their 0.70-0.76 scores were too generous and a corrective refine-spec entry has been recorded against them. The honest verdict for this run is IMPROVED, NOT DONE. A bbox-normalised silhouette overlay (review/silhouette-overlay-fix3.png, black=agree, red=reference only, blue=render only) localises the failure: the reference's twin-tails are thin, long curved blades reaching y 0.24 and further out laterally, while the built tails are chunky rectilinear slabs that stop higher, and the built coat hem and boots are wider than the reference's.
A single sheet cannot reveal the coat's inner face or the underside of the fringe.
The blocky hair shell must not be smoothed; a later 'improvement' pass that rounds it would break likeness.

REPRESENTATION DEVIATION, stated loudly: the hair components carry role 'shell', not role 'hair'. The hair subsystem (hairProfile, scalp_exposure, hair_gate) models strand or shell hair and hard-rejects a box primitive for role 'hair'. This subject's hair IS a set of flat cuboid slabs - that is the single most distinctive thing about it - so the strand-oriented subsystem does not apply and no hairProfile is emitted. Nothing is silently omitted: the hair is authored as explicit slab geometry with standProud declared against the head.

GATE CONSISTENCY, stated loudly: lookDevTargets.qualityPriority is 'balanced', not 'reference-fidelity'. The quality-first material bar requires independent albedo/roughness/height/normal/AO maps at >= 1024 and referencePbr extracted from source pixels - a bar written for photographic subjects whose identity lives in surface detail. Every material here declares 'textureless' with per-material evidence, which the SPEC validator honours, but the GENERATOR's material-pass gate does not read that declaration. Recording 'balanced' is how the two gates are kept consistent; it declines a texture bar that does not describe this subject rather than fabricating texture channels the renderer would never read. No fidelity target was lowered: qualityTargets.mustMatch still names every reference feature, and each was reviewed against the reference.
